title: When Coverage Attaches: Waiting Period Rules of the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
## Standard rule

New business and every mid-term coverage increase or deductible decrease on the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own) take effect at 12:01 a.m. on the day that is the tier's standard waiting period in calendar days after the date the signed application (or endorsement request) and the full premium are received, counted by adding the days to that receipt date on the calendar, and the waiting-period basis recorded is standard.

## Statutory exceptions

Two statutory exceptions replace the standard wait, and only one basis is recorded per transaction.

**Loan transaction.** The coverage is bought or increased in connection with making, increasing, extending or renewing a loan secured by the building. The loan-transaction exception applies only when the application and full premium are received no later than the date the loan closes; coverage then takes effect at the loan closing date, the waiting-period basis is loan transaction and the loan closing date is recorded.

**Map revision.** The building was newly placed in a Special Flood Hazard Area by a revision of the Flood Insurance Rate Map. The map-revision exception applies only when the application and full premium are received no later than the tier's map-revision window in calendar months after the map revision that placed the building in a Special Flood Hazard Area takes effect; coverage then takes effect at 12:01 a.m. on the day after receipt (the map-revision waiting period), the waiting-period basis is map revision and the map revision date is recorded. The window is counted by adding calendar months to the map revision effective date, falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist, and a receipt on the last day of the window qualifies.

When both exceptions could apply, the one giving the earlier effective date is recorded.

## Decreases and losses

Coverage decreases and deductible increases are never effective mid-term; they are accepted only effective on a renewal date. A loss that begins before the effective date of the coverage, or of an increase, is not covered by that coverage or increase.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates; window and waits from the effective-date figures)

| Situation | Receipt of application and full premium | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Loan closes 15 May | 15 May | exception applies — receipt on the closing date is not later than it; coverage at the loan closing date |
| Loan closes 15 May | 16 May | exception does not apply — received after the closing date |
| Map revision effective 31 January, 13-month window | 28 February of the following year (no 31 February) | qualifies — the window falls back to the last day of that month, and a receipt on the last day qualifies |
| Same map revision | 1 March of the following year | does not qualify |

The evidence for each exception is the date on the policy record — the loan closing date or the map revision date — set against the receipt date; the caller's account of a loan or a map change is checked against those recorded dates.
